PullRequest.Title: Single chat migrations setting
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request consolidates multiple migration settings into a single configuration option to simplify the migration process. The new setting, `chat.customizations.migration.enabled`, replaces the previous five individual settings, streamlining the migration behavior across the application.

Key changes include:

- Introduced a single migration setting: `chat.customizations.migration.enabled` (default: `true`).
- Removed the previous individual migration settings for locations, MCP server, prompts, user data, and migration hints.
- Updated relevant constants and contribution registrations to reflect the new unified setting.
- Adjusted migration behavior to ensure all related features are enabled or disabled based on the new setting.
- Modified tests and fixtures to accommodate the changes in migration settings.

Validation steps have been completed, including passing ESLint checks and successful client transpilation. All legacy setting references have been removed, and focused unit tests are prepared for execution.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed gate, production default=true, awaited sendRequest call path, 50 ms MCP debounce, filesystem reads, and empty-result repetition are all directly established in repository code. Actual added latency beyond the guaranteed debounce varies with MCP initialization, remote filesystem speed, configured roots, and source count.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Filesystem discovery/read operations, MCP support assessment CPU work, and the 50 ms support-scope debounce
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cold work scans up to four prompt types across user and workspace locations; MCP plan reads once per distinct eligible source configuration. When no candidates are found, this entire hint computation is re-entered once per chat message, and remote/configured locations increase I/O latency.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocks agent dispatch and increases time to first response on each affected chat message, with additional I/O and CPU pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The old chat.customizations.migrationHint setting defaulted to Never, so ordinary agent-host requests returned before computeMigrationHint. MCP, user-data, and configured-location migrations also defaulted disabled.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed condition uses chat.customizations.migration.enabled, registered with default true, so ordinary requests now await full migration discovery; an empty result does not mark discovery as completed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line 1699 replaces the prior hint-mode check (whose default was Never) with ChatCustomizationsMigrationEnabled; the unified setting is registered default true in this diff.
Findings.Title: Keep migration discovery off every empty chat request
Findings.Impact: With the new setting's production default of true, every Copilot agent-host request enters computeMigrationHint before the agent is activated. If no migration candidate exists, customizationMigrationHintShown is never set, so the same discovery runs again on every subsequent message, delaying agent invocation and time to first response.
Findings.Evidence: sendRequest awaits collectCustomizationMigrationHint in its Step 2 Promise.all before extension activation/agent invocation. computeMigrationHint concurrently scans user/workspace prompt files for agent, instructions, prompt, and skill types and invokes the MCP migration provider. That provider creates an AgentHostMcpServerSupportScope whose first resolution is deliberately delayed 50 ms, waits for initial MCP loading, and createPlan reads each distinct MCP source configuration via IFileService. The provider disposes the scope after each computation; the scope disposes at refcount zero, so absent another holder there is no warm MCP assessment to reuse. Prompt listings are cached/coalesced per type, but the MCP assessment/config reads repeat. The request state is committed only when a nonempty hint is shown, leaving the common empty result uncached.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve a separately default-off hint/discovery gate, or cache/coalesce the empty assessment with invalidation from onDidChangeCustomizations and run it outside the request-dispatch critical path. Ensure a request can invoke the agent without awaiting migration UI discovery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a message in a Copilot agent-host chat session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: sendRequest creates the visible request, then awaits hooks, instructions, and customization migration discovery together before extension activation and agent invocation. The migration branch therefore delays dispatch even though it only produces an informational hint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt/customization files in user and workspace locations for agent, instructions, prompt, and skill types.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to four distinct prompt-type discoveries per assessment, each covering user and local locations and all configured source folders; concurrent duplicate type requests can reuse a cached promise when that type's cache is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old chat hint setting defaulted to Never, so the normal request path did not invoke migration discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the agent request can be dispatched.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse MCP source configuration files while creating migration candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per distinct eligible MCP source URI per assessment, deduplicated within that single plan only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: MCP migration and chat hints both defaulted disabled, so this read was absent from ordinary sends.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by computeMigrationHint and therefore blocks agent dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and resolve MCP support scope, including a 50 ms debounce and waiting for initial local MCP server loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scope resolution per hint assessment when no other consumer retains the keyed scope; the migration provider releases it after each computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Default-disabled hints returned before acquiring this scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds at least the scheduled debounce for a newly created scope before agent dispatch, plus MCP loading/assessment time.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chat messages when no migration exists, plus configured prompt locations, workspace roots, and distinct MCP source files. Empty assessments are not marked shown, so frequency scales per message rather than once per session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Four migration categories run in Promise.all; prompt discovery also fans out user/local searches. There is per-type promise caching for warm prompt discovery, but no cross-request cache/coalescing for the MCP assessment after its last scope reference is released.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt lists may be cached and invalidated by file events. MCP source reads are deduplicated only within one plan. No negative cache records an empty migration hint, so empty results repeat on every request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: changed default-enabled gate, awaited call path, boundary operations, disposal behavior, and empty-result repetition are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and MCP initialization duration varies by local/remote environment and configured sources; the support-scope 50 ms debounce and pre-dispatch placement are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: default-enabled migration discovery adds repeated I/O and a support-resolution wait to the chat response critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh the Chat Customizations management editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor renders and starts refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo without awaiting it; migration dashboard results/loading wait on enabled-category discovery, but base editor opening can progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List candidate files for enabled migration categories and read eligible MCP source configurations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Default now enables prompt files, user-data, and MCP categories; configured-location discovery additionally runs only when one of its location settings differs from default. Category calls are concurrent and file-list caches can serve overlapping types.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: By default only prompt-file migration was enabled; user-data, configured-location, and MCP categories were separately default-off.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Controls completion of migration cards/dashboard, not initial editor construction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled categories, configured locations, customization file count, and distinct MCP source files; refreshes are triggered by prompt/MCP/session changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Enabled categories execute in Promise.all. Refreshes use a delayer, sequence guard, and cancellation store, limiting stale application but not category-level I/O concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt lists use per-type promise caches with event invalidation. MCP support scope can be reused only while another consumer holds it; source reads are per plan.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the additional default-enabled work and boundary calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor users and source counts vary, and the work is asynchronous/off the base editor critical path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: added work is bounded, asynchronous, and directly supplies the newly enabled migration UI; the critical-path chat invocation is the actionable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show migration availability in Sessions navigation or a chat migration notice
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Autoruns launch computeMigrationHint asynchronously after session/context/configuration changes. Navigation and notice visibility wait for discovery, but session operation itself does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover customization files and plan MCP migrations through computeMigrationHint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full assessment per triggering autorun instance; separate navigation/notice consumers are not coalesced with one another, while prompt-service caches reduce warm file scans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These consumers already assessed prompt-file migration by default; the diff broadens each assessment to newly enabled categories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only availability/notice rendering waits; core session navigation remains usable.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active notice/navigation consumers and customization-change events, plus configured locations/MCP sources.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each consumer has cancellation tied to its autorun lifetime, but there is no shared assessment promise across consumers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm prompt lists are reusable; MCP planning and empty-hint results are not shared across consumers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for expanded work, lower concern because it is off the main workflow critical path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Concurrent consumer prevalence and remote I/O duration are uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: bounded asynchronous visibility work, with the more consequential request-path regression already reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: View MCP server list/detail compatibility diagnostics
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the MCP list or an installed server detail is visible, the widget acquires a compatibility scope and updates badges/details asynchronously; hiding/rebinding disposes the scope.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assess MCP server compatibility and wait for initial local MCP server metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One keyed support scope per visible list/detail consumer, reference-counted and shared for matching session/root keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The separately default-false MCP migration setting prevented scope acquisition for most users.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Compatibility badges/details can remain in checking state; list/detail rendering itself proceeds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously visible MCP views and MCP servers; keyed scopes share assessment for the same context.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reference-counted scopes coalesce matching consumers and debounce updates; scopes are disposed at zero references.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Scope state is warm while visible/retained and removed when the final consumer releases it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lifecycle and default activation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Compatibility assessment cost depends on MCP server count and initialization state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: work is visible-feature-driven, shared by key, asynchronous, and cleaned up on hide/disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Register and evaluate the consolidated migration configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration registration occurs during contribution setup; reads of the boolean are in-memory and do not cross an expensive boundary.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant number of configuration entries/read checks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous work at registration itself.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration service supplies the registered default and experiment override; no new application cache is involved.
Scenarios.Verdict: No direct startup finding; the performance effect comes from downstream paths now activated by the default-true setting.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 17 changed files. One medium-severity eager-work regression was reported: the unified default-enabled setting moves full migration discovery, including a fresh 50 ms-debounced MCP assessment and filesystem reads, onto every empty agent-host chat request before agent dispatch. Other expanded migration/compatibility work is asynchronous, bounded, cache-aware or scope-coalesced enough not to justify separate findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
